newsitem.title: UK: North Sea wet market quiet but differentials firm.
newsitem.headline: North Sea wet market quiet but differentials firm.

text.p: The North Sea physical market was quiet as sellers held out for higher differentials in a tight market driven higher by a futures rally, traders said.
Two Brent cargoes loading in the third decade traded at November +10 cents and brokers expected North Sea grades to fetch higher premiums.
"The next cargo will be done at a few cents more than the one before, particularly for gas oil grades," a broker said.
The only Brent cargo in the paper chains on Monday was kept ahead of the five o'clock deadline by an equity holder, giving further evidence of market strength.

With Forties basically cleared out for October and three of the five remaining Oseberg cargoes in the hands of the producer, the next deal on the gas oil grade was expected to be done at Dated Brent +50 cents.
Outright 15-day Brent values soared in line with screen values. November Brent paper was talked around $24-$24.05 compared with Friday's close of $23.70 a barrel.
December Brent traded at $23.57 and $23.62 with Nov/Dec last done at +52 cents after an earlier deal one cent lower.
The Med was quiet with no Urals seen done since last Wednesday.
The grade was seen well-offered and unlikely to achieve offered levels of Dated Brent -65 cents cif.
"It is dead quiet. People are only playing on the screen. That is the focus of attention," a Med refinery trader said.
"Obviously Urals sellers are hoping to get closer to 65 under but the market is closer to -70/-75 cents of thereabouts," she added.

The West African market was very quiet with lifters still waiting for confirmation on cargoes. Some Nigerian light grades, Palanca or Oseberg were seen moving into a Lagoven tender for 500,000 barrels of sweet crude into NWE, trader said.
